Two-stage garment → mannequin spike

Hypothesis: the single call asks the image model to do too much at once. Stage 1 reconstructs the GARMENT ALONE — no body — from the raw Product Truth plus a background-free SAM2 cutout. Stage 2 then dresses the existing fixed mannequin with that reconstruction, with the original photographs still the final authority on every product fact. The control is the existing raw → mannequin output, reused, not regenerated. 6 image calls, 0 provider failures, 1 new SAM2 run. No QC, no correction, no retries. Cutout masks are HUMAN_SELECTED_EXPERIMENTAL_MASK — not production automation. Verdicts are a person's.

stripeStage 1: GOODFinal: TWO_STAGE_BETTER

Overall: TWO_STAGE_PROMISING

Both Stage-1 boards preserve the real garment, and on both products the two-stage mannequin keeps more of it than the direct baseline: the stripe keeps its second colour, and 4ff2132f loses the control's invented neck button and label. Two products, one generation per stage — enough to justify a larger test, not enough to justify integration. The stripe's rear geometry is unverifiable because its Back photograph does not show a rear view, and the masks were picked by hand.

STRIPE shirt — cropped/boxy, collar, front placket, buttons, fine muted vertical stripe

gemini-3-pro-image · 4K · stage 1 49271 ms · stage 2 37854 ms · 2 image calls

Stage 1 garment reconstruction GOOD

Three consistent views of one product. Collar, full front placket and every button present; cropped boxy length kept; cuffs and back yoke correct. The stripe is fine, vertical and muted, with the taupe and the blue both present and not widened — the failure that has dogged this product through every earlier experiment did NOT happen here.

Final two-stage vs RAW baseline TWO_STAGE_BETTER

The control renders warm beige stripes with the blue gone; the two-stage result keeps both colours and the finer density, on a cooler ground much closer to the source. Collar, placket and buttons equivalent in both. The two-stage body is fractionally longer than the cropped source.

BACK_CUTOUT_UNAVAILABLE_SOURCE_LIMITATION — BACK_CUTOUT_UNAVAILABLE_SOURCE_LIMITATION — the Back photograph is a tight crop of the crumpled garment: no full rear silhouette, hem out of frame, sleeves cut off. No cutout was fabricated from it; the raw Back photograph is still supplied to Stage 1 as supporting product evidence.

4ff2132f — round scoop neck, curved yoke seam with gathering, short cap sleeves, dusty-mauve pointelle knit, flared hem

gemini-3-pro-image · 1K · stage 1 27014 ms · stage 2 19426 ms · 2 image calls

Stage 1 garment reconstruction GOOD

Round scoop neckline (not square), curved yoke seam with gathering below it, short cap sleeves with no cuff band, dusty-mauve base colour and a clearly rendered pointelle openwork surface, with a slightly flared hem. This is the first render in the whole investigation that holds neckline, colour AND pointelle at the same time.

Final two-stage vs RAW baseline TWO_STAGE_BETTER

Both keep the round neck and the mauve. The control invents a button and an outward-hanging label at the centre neck that the product does not have; the two-stage result has neither, and its yoke seam is a single clean curve with the gathering below it. Pointelle visible in both.
